questions.question: What makes adversarial testing different from a standard safety benchmark?
options: It uses only public prompts and one aggregate score.
It searches adaptively for credible system failures under an explicit threat model.
It proves that no future attacker can succeed.
It tests only the base model without application context.
questions.explanation: Adversarial testing follows an attacker model through real product boundaries and adapts to observed defenses. It does not prove the absence of future attacks.

questions.question: Why is an indirect prompt injection a system-level concern?
options: It changes only the font used to display model output.
It requires access to model gradients.
It can enter through retrieved or tool-returned content rather than the user's direct prompt.
It can be prevented completely by adding more retrieval documents.
questions.explanation: Indirect instructions arrive through data the application asks the model to consume. The application must preserve provenance and enforce authority outside model text.

questions.question: A retrieved document influences a proposed account change. Which control most directly prevents the document from authorizing the effect?
options: A larger context window.
A higher model temperature.
A more detailed hidden prompt alone.
A deterministic authorization check using user identity, purpose, and tool policy.
questions.explanation: The model may propose an action, but an external authorization layer must decide whether the identified user and purpose permit it.

questions.question: A candidate has a low aggregate attack-success rate but fails one critical tool-authorization slice. What should a severity-aware gate do?
options: Hold or restrict the release because the critical slice remains blocking.
Pass because common moderate cases dilute the failure.
Delete the failing slice from the corpus.
Average attack success with latency.
questions.explanation: Different harms are not interchangeable units. A healthy aggregate cannot cancel a failure that crosses a critical authorization boundary.

questions.question: Why must adversarial evaluation include benign cases?
options: To make every attack success count as a true positive.
To remove the need for severity labels.
To measure whether defenses overblock legitimate use or reduce product utility.
To guarantee that human reviewers agree.
questions.explanation: A defense can reduce attack success by denying too much legitimate use. False positives and utility floors expose that cost.

questions.question: What should happen after a confirmed adversarial production incident is contained?
options: Store all raw user data permanently in a public benchmark.
Create a minimized, access-controlled regression tied to the affected boundary and release gate.
Remove the related telemetry to prevent future alerts.
Treat the fix as permanent even when system versions change.
questions.explanation: A minimized regression preserves the failure mechanism without retaining unnecessary sensitive or operational exploit detail.

questions.question: Why should a team rerun attacks after adding a detector or prompt defense?
options: A defense makes the original system version impossible to identify.
Every detector has exactly the same false-positive rate.
Static tests always overestimate risk.
An adaptive attacker changes strategy after observing the defense.
questions.explanation: A static corpus measures known attempts. Adaptive evaluation probes whether the mitigation actually changes the reachable attack paths.

questions.question: Which disclosure record best supports responsible remediation?
options: Affected versions, boundary, impact, minimized reproduction, owner, containment, and coordinated publication status.
A public dump of live credentials and successful payloads.
Only a screenshot of the final model response.
An unversioned statement that the model is robust.
questions.explanation: A useful disclosure supports verification and coordination while minimizing sensitive data and details that would increase exploitation risk.
